summary_html: **Healthcare encounters** that reveal suspected abuse or neglect trigger reporting obligations. Federal law governs mandatory reporting in federal facilities and coordination with state systems.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — state reporter systems and protections  
- **Victims of Child Abuse Act (34 U.S.C. §§ 20301–20307)** — mandates in federal settings, CAC coordination

primary_citations.citation_text: Illinois - 325 ILCS 5 (Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act)
Illinois - 705 ILCS 405/2 (Juvenile Court Act – abuse/neglect proceedings)
Title 325: Children (ILCS 325) - DCFS - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the appellate court's reversal of a neglect adjudication, holding that a mother who left her children with a boyfriend she had no reason to suspect, and who took the injured child straight to hospital, did not place them in an injurious environment.
key_cases.relevance: The neglect finding rested in part on Pediatric Resource Center medical records generated after a hospital presentation.
key_cases.quote: If the State fails to prove the allegations of abuse, neglect, or dependence by a preponderance of the evidence, the court must dismiss the petition.

key_cases.holding: The court held that at an adjudicatory hearing the circuit court must focus solely on whether the child was neglected rather than apportion blame among parents, and, finding the State had failed to prove neglect as to Arthur Jr., reversed the circuit court and dismissed the amended wardship petition.
key_cases.relevance: The neglect allegations rested on medical-neglect findings reported by a DCFS investigator after a health-care contact, and the court held that evidence insufficient.
key_cases.quote: It is the burden of the State to prove allegations of neglect by a preponderance of the evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the neglect adjudication and wardship of a newborn, holding Illinois had jurisdiction under the UCCJEA even though the child was delivered in Indiana, that the ex parte shelter-care notice complaint was moot, and that the injurious-environment finding was not against the manifest weight of the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: The case arose from the mother's flight from Illinois against her obstetrician's instructions and the out-of-state hospital delivery that followed.
key_cases.quote: On review, a trial court's ruling of neglect will not be reversed unless it is against the manifest weight of the evidence.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a minor shown by clear and convincing evidence to be mature has a common-law right to consent to or refuse medical treatment, subject to countervailing state interests, and remanded with directions to expunge the neglect finding entered against the minor's mother.
key_cases.relevance: The case reached the juvenile court through the hospital treating a seventeen-year-old leukemia patient who refused blood transfusions.
key_cases.quote: Because we find that a mature minor may exercise a common law right to consent to or refuse medical care, we decline to address the constitutional issue.

search_keywords: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

state_agency.name: Illinois Department of Children and Family Services

mandatory_reporters: Medical personnel — physicians, residents, interns, psychiatrists, surgeons, dentists, dental hygienists, chiropractic and podiatric physicians, physician assistants, emergency medical technicians, physical and occupational therapists, acupuncturists, registered/licensed practical/advanced practice nurses, genetic counselors, respiratory care practitioners, home health aides, certified nursing assistants — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(1)

Social services and mental health personnel — licensed counselors, social workers, psychologists, marriage and family therapists, field personnel of Healthcare and Family Services, Public Health, Human Services, Human Rights and DCFS, General Assistance supervisors/administrators, social services administrators, substance abuse treatment personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(2)
Crisis intervention personnel — crisis line or hotline personnel, domestic violence program personnel — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(3)

Education personnel — school personnel (administrators, certified and non-certified employees), personnel of institutions of higher education, educational advocates, school board members (to the extent required by subsection (d)), truant officers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(4)
Recreation or athletic program or facility personnel; athletic trainers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(5)
Child care personnel — early intervention providers, nursery school and early care and education center directors and staff, foster parents, homemakers, child care workers — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(6)

Law enforcement personnel — law enforcement officers, Department of Juvenile Justice and Department of Corrections field personnel, probation officers, animal control officers and Department of Agriculture field investigators — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(7)
Funeral home directors and employees; coroners; medical examiners — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(8)
Any member of the clergy — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(9)
Medical, nursing, social work and counseling personnel of any office or clinic that provides abortions, abortion referrals, or contraceptives — 325 ILCS 5/4(a)(10)
reporting_details: Illinois is not a universal-reporting state: only the professionals listed in 325 ILCS 5/4(a) must report, any other person may report voluntarily under 325 ILCS 5/4(f), and every report goes to the single statewide DCFS hotline required by 325 ILCS 5/7.6 (1-800-25-ABUSE / 1-800-252-2873).

timeline_requirements.deadline: 24 hours; immediately, regardless of the time of day or night, if the child's immediate safety or well-being is endangered or the family may flee (325 ILCS 5/7.4(b)(2))
60 days to determine "indicated" or "unfounded"; extendable in additional periods of up to 30 days for good cause (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Report may be deemed "undetermined" where a complete investigation was not possible (325 ILCS 5/7.12)
